answer: An agent earns a billing identity only after cutting a living cedar spar, turning it into a directional horn, and planting that horn on a surveyed stake in a shifting river delta. The registrar later pings the horn at an unannounced tide, and the return signal must match the spar's ring-density acoustic fingerprint plus the stake's tide datum. Reused horns or stakes collapse to one operator and get slashed. Forging N identities therefore costs N living trees, N surveyed delta plots, and N real acoustic pings through changing water.
